headline: The Dow bottomed out in July, Roosevelt won in November, and Hitler became a German citizen in February
texture: The Dow Jones reached its lowest point of the entire slump on July 8, having lost most of what it was worth in 1929. Franklin Roosevelt, governor of New York, won the presidency on November 8. The Nazis remained the largest party in the Reichstag after the election on November 6, without a majority, and Hitler had only obtained German citizenship on February 25, which was what let him stand for office at all.

Charles Lindbergh's infant son was taken from the family home in March and the search ran for months. Amelia Earhart flew the Atlantic alone on May 20 and 21, landing in County Londonderry, five years after Lindbergh had done it. General Kurt von Schleicher met Hitler in secret in May, and there were violent scenes in the Reichstag chamber the same month.

The Sign of the Cross led the box office at $2,738,993 in rentals, with The Kid from Spain close behind. Grand Hotel was fifth and won Best Picture. Lake Placid held the Winter Olympics in February and Los Angeles the summer games. John Philip Sousa died on March 6 and Edgar Wallace in February, a month after finishing the story that became King Kong.

notes: Research pass July 2026. No prices section: the three price series all start later. Three claims are general knowledge of their subjects rather than statements from the year pages, and come out if challenged: that Grand Hotel was nominated in no other category, that Edgar Wallace had just finished the King Kong story, and that double features spread because of the price. The unemployment figure in the mood line is the commonly cited quarter and carries no source, which is why it sits in a section that requires none.
